SmolVLA on LIBERO

Final A100 cost curve

Every panel uses the same scale. Points are 20 rollout episodes for each of two training seeds; lines show their mean. No run is hidden.

Old proxy results

Every measured method is visible. Lines exist only when the same method was evaluated at several demonstration budgets. These runs used the old proxy dataset.

Training dynamics

Every run starts at 1.0. The shared logarithmic scale shows relative optimization progress despite different loss definitions. Episode-mask and padding-mask losses are omitted because they are identical in every recorded step.

Action error on fixed target-demo frames

Mean absolute error over three frames, every chunk step, and seven action coordinates. Lower means the checkpoint fits these demonstration frames better; this is not held-out rollout quality.

Fine-tuning cost versus target-demo fit

Only the four directly comparable fine-tuning choices are shown. Left trains fewer parameters; lower reconstructs the recorded actions better. The x-axis is logarithmic.

Naive and longer train the same action expert; longer only doubles the steps. Full also trains the VLM and vision encoder. LoRA trains adapters while the base weights stay frozen.

Image augmentations used in training

Each frame receives three of six transforms: brightness and contrast 0.8 to 1.2, saturation 0.5 to 1.5, hue -0.05 to 0.05, sharpness 0.5 to 1.5, or affine rotation ±5° with translation up to 5%.

Predicted action chunks

Seven action coordinates are shown together on the same [-1, 1] scale. Black is the demonstrated target. Chunk 10 ends after step 9 by design.

Rejected raw visual-residual predictor

This first implementation predicted the full visual-token residual directly. It remains here as a failed experiment.

Continuous LAPO tiny-set gate

The inverse model compresses each adjacent visual-token pair into 32 values. The forward model must reconstruct the token change from the current frame and this latent.
